resources.title: The address that would not update
resources.body: A college office stores each student address in five different registers. A student moves house.

resources.title: In simple words
resources.body:
Normalization means splitting one big table into smaller tables so that each fact is stored only once and nothing gets out of sync.

> **Think of it like this:** Like keeping one master attendance register instead of copies in every classroom.

resources.title: Where this is used
resources.body:
- Banking systems keep one customer record.
- Railway reservation stores trains once.
- College ERP keeps one student table.

resources.title: 10-mark answer: Normalization
resources.body:
**Definition.** Normalization organises tables to reduce redundancy.

**Need.** Redundant data causes update, insertion and deletion anomalies.

**Explanation**

1. **1NF**: Atomic values and no repeating groups.
2. **2NF**: No partial dependency on a composite key.
3. **3NF**: No transitive dependency between non-key attributes.

**Example / diagram.** Split Student(Roll, Name, Dept, HOD) into Student(Roll, Name, Dept) and Dept(Dept, HOD).

**Advantages**

- Less redundancy
- No anomalies

**Conclusion.** Normalization keeps data consistent through lossless decomposition.

resources.title: Normalise a mess sheet
resources.body:
1. Take the sample mess-bill sheet. 2. List its functional dependencies. 3. Split it into 3NF tables.

**Submit:** A PDF with your tables and dependencies.
